The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1a8212bf07eeb82d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 26. statement: Identify real Lipschitz functions on Y that agree µ-almost everywhere. Their completion in the norm ∥u∥2 H = ∥u∥2 2 + E(u) is a Hilbert space H of functions in L2(µ). Its gradient is a well-defined closed operator with values in the Hilbert space of square-integrable chart covectors. The inclusion H ⟶ Lp(µ) is continuous, and (4.22) holds for all u ∈ H. The following calculus properties hold. (i) If u1, . . . , uk ∈ H and Φ ∈ C1(Rk) has bounded first derivatives, then Φ(u1, . . . , uk) ∈ H and DΦ(u1, . . . , uk) = k ∑ a=1 ∂aΦ(u1, . . . , uk)Dua. (ii) For every u ∈ H and every fixed t ∈ R, Du = 0 almost everywhere on {u = t}. Consequently, the scalar chain rule also holds for Lipschitz, piecewise C1 functions with finitely many corners, with any derivative values assigned at the corners. (iii) The map u ↦ u+ is continuous from H to itself. Every nonnegative element of H has nonnegative Lipschitz approximants converging in H. (iv) For each fixed center y ∈ Y , the radial inequality (3.1) holds for every nonnegative g ∈ H, with r = d(y, ·) and its chart gradient Dr.
